memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob said, 'Please tell me your name.' But he replied, 'Why do you ask my name?' Then he blessed him there. So Jacob called the place Peniel, saying, 'It is because I saw God face to face, and yet my life was spared.'" - Gen 32:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As dawn breaks, Jacob asks the mysterious man for his name, but receives only a blessing in reply. Yet Jacob knows what has happened. He names the place Peniel — "the face of God" — and says in wonder, "I saw God face to face, and yet my life was spared." Jacob realises he has not merely wrestled with a man; he has encountered God Himself in some visible form, and lived to tell of it.

To meet the holy God face to face is an overwhelming thing. Scripture teaches that God's glory is so great that no sinful person could see Him fully and survive (Ex 33:20). So Jacob is amazed: he met God and was not consumed. Grace had spared him. What could have been his destruction became his blessing.

There is a wonder here that points us forward. The face-to-face nearness that so amazed Jacob is offered to us fully in Jesus. "No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son... has made him known" (John 1:18). In Christ, God has drawn near to us with a human face, so that we can know Him and not be destroyed but saved.

The God who met Jacob at Peniel invites you into His presence too — not to consume you, but to bless you. Through Christ, we can come near to God and live. Draw near, and be amazed at His grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I amazed at the grace that lets me come near to a holy God?
2. How does knowing God in Christ shape my sense of His presence?
3. Where do I need to draw near to God and receive His blessing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that through Christ I can come near to You and live. I am amazed at the grace that spares me and blesses me. Draw me into Your presence, and let me know You. Amen.
